editorial:
Imagine walking into your dad's 70th birthday party only to find out your youngest sibling wrote a tell-all book about your family's dirtiest secrets. That is exactly the mess you get into with this movie. You follow four siblings who all have very different personalities, but they all share the same trauma and family baggage. The vibe is a mix of awkward laughs and heavy arguments. It feels like one of those family dinners that starts off polite but ends up with everyone screaming, making you feel like you are sitting right there in the room with them.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the cast does a great job making the fighting feel real. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow while they talk through their issues. If you love character studies and family drama, you will enjoy this. It is a great pick if you want something that feels human and honest.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during the party when the siblings finally stop pretending to be perfect. They confront the youngest sibling about the book, but they also realize that their father was not the hero they thought he was. Instead of staying angry, they start to accept their shared flaws. The movie ends with the family finding a weird kind of peace, knowing that their secrets are out and they can finally stop lying to each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dysfunctional family stories and witty dialogue.
